head: 16a54f0f85a9091f220418850eac6b4122782be5
title: fix: guard against ReDoS via user-controlled regex in custom rules engine
body:
## Summary

- Reject patterns longer than 1 000 characters in `CustomRulesEngine.validatePattern()`, preventing oversized regex from reaching the engine
- Allowlist regex flags to `gimsuy` characters only in `validatePattern()`, blocking invalid or dangerous flag strings
- Strip disallowed flag characters at `executePattern()` runtime as a defense-in-depth measure for rules loaded directly from `.techdebtrc.json` (bypassing `validatePattern`)
- Export `MAX_CODE_LENGTH` (500 000) from `customRulesEngine.ts` and enforce it in `parseExecuteCustomRulesInput()` to cap the inline `code` parameter, preventing an unbounded string from being fed through every custom rule regex
- Update `CHANGELOG.md` with the security fix entry

Closes #127

## Test plan
- [x] `validatePattern` rejects patterns > 1 000 chars with a descriptive error
- [x] `validatePattern` accepts patterns exactly at the 1 000-char boundary
- [x] `validatePattern` rejects flags containing any character outside `gimsuy`
- [x] `validatePattern` accepts all six valid flag characters (`gimsuy`)
- [x] `executePattern` strips disallowed flags at runtime without throwing, still matches correctly
- [x] `parseExecuteCustomRulesInput` throws `McpError` when `code` exceeds 500 000 characters
- [x] `parseExecuteCustomRulesInput` accepts `code` exactly at the 500 000-character limit
- [x] All 538 existing tests continue to pass
- [x] TypeScript build succeeds (`npm run build`)

head: 41d750067fc7a39eb29f6a530cf0d4ae0f8bdb41
title: feat: pluggable auth providers — add AT Protocol, refactor GitHub/Google
body: ## What does this PR do? Introduces a **pluggable auth provider system** and uses it to add **AT Protocol authentication** as the first plugin-based provider. GitHub and Google OAuth are refactored from hardcoded buttons into the same provider interface. All auth methods — passkey, AT Protocol, GitHub, Google — are equal options on the login page and setup wizard. ### Auth provider descriptor Every provider implements `AuthProviderDescriptor`: ```ts emdash({ authProviders: [atproto(), github(), google()], }) ``` Each descriptor declares an `adminEntry` (React components for login/setup UI), optional `routes` (Astro route handlers), and `publicRoutes` (middleware bypass prefixes). Components are distributed to the admin app via a `virtual:emdash/auth-providers` Vite virtual module. ### What changed > **Scope note:** The entire pluggable auth provider system is new in this PR — none of it existed on `main`. The pre-existing `AuthDescriptor` / `AuthProviderModule` (transparent auth for Cloudflare Access) is unchanged. **New pluggable infrastructure (core):** - `AuthProviderDescriptor` / `AuthRouteDescriptor` types in `auth/types.ts` - `authProviders` config field on `EmDashConfig` - `virtual:emdash/auth-providers` virtual module with `generateAuthProvidersModule()` - `injectAuthProviderRoutes()` for generic route injection from descriptors - Dynamic public routes in auth middleware (merged from all providers) - `AuthProviderContext` in admin for distributing provider UI components - Public `/_emdash/api/auth/mode` endpoint returning available providers - `emdash/api/route-utils` public export for API utilities used by plugin routes - `finalizeSetup()` shared helper for setup completion (idempotent, used by all auth callbacks) **Shared OAuth user creation (`@emdash-cms/auth`):** - `findOrCreateOAuthUser()` extracted as a shared export — handles OAuth account lookup, email auto-linking, and user creation with `canSelfSignup` policy - Used by all OAuth providers (GitHub, Google, AT Protocol) for consistent signup gating and role assignment **Login page:** - Removed hardcoded `OAUTH_PROVIDERS` array - All providers render from virtual module via `useAuthProviderList()` - Providers with `LoginButton` show in a button grid; those with `LoginForm` expand inline on click **Setup wizard:** - All configured auth providers appear as equal options alongside passkey - Clicking a provider button either navigates directly (GitHub/Google OAuth) or expands a form (AT Protocol handle input) - OAuth callback is setup-aware: first user becomes admin, site config is persisted, setup is marked complete - First-user admin creation uses a database transaction to prevent TOCTOU race conditions - URL error params displayed in a banner (previously errors were silently lost) **AT Protocol (new — `@emdash-cms/plugin-atproto`):** - `atproto()` returns `AuthProviderDescriptor` with routes for login, callback, setup-admin, and client metadata - Route handlers live in the plugin package (`@emdash-cms/plugin-atproto/routes/*`), not in core — removing the plugin removes the routes - `LoginButton` (compact butterfly icon), `LoginForm` (handle input), `SetupStep` exported from `@emdash-cms/plugin-atproto/admin` - Uses `@atcute/oauth-node-client` with PKCE (public client, no key management needed) - First user becomes Admin during setup; subsequent users get the configured default role (Subscriber by default) - `allowedDIDs` allowlist for access control by permanent DID identifiers - `allowedHandles` allowlist with wildcard support for org-level domain gating (e.g., `*.mycompany.com`). Handle ownership is independently verified via DNS-over-HTTPS and HTTP well-known resolution using `@atcute/identity-resolver` — the PDS's handle claim is never trusted directly - If both are set, matching either list grants access - Uses shared `findOrCreateOAuthUser()` with `canSelfSignup` policy for consistent signup gating **GitHub / Google (refactored to descriptors):** - `github()` and `google()` return `AuthProviderDescriptor` with `adminEntry` pointing to `-admin.tsx` components - `LoginButton` components with provider icons, reusing core's existing `[provider]` OAuth routes - No new routes needed — they reuse core's shared OAuth infrastructure **OAuth error handling:** - OAuth initiation route checks `Referer` to redirect errors back to the originating page (setup wizard vs login) - Error messages include which env vars need to be set when a provider isn't configured ### Configuration ```ts import { atproto } from "@emdash-cms/plugin-atproto/auth"; import { github } from "emdash/auth/providers/github"; import { google } from "emdash/auth/providers/google"; emdash({ authProviders: [atproto(), github(), google()], }) ``` AT Protocol options: ```ts atproto({ // Permanent DID-based allowlist allowedDIDs: ["did:plc:abc123"], // Domain-based allowlist (independently verified via DNS/HTTP) allowedHandles: ["*.mycompany.com", "alice.bsky.social"], // Default role for new users (default: 10 / Subscriber) defaultRole: 20, // Contributor }) ``` ### New routes (AT Protocol) - `POST /_emdash/api/auth/atproto/login` — initiate OAuth flow (handle → PDS authorization URL) - `GET /_emdash/api/auth/atproto/callback` — handle PDS redirect, create/find user, establish session - `POST /_emdash/api/setup/atproto-admin` — setup wizard flow - `GET /.well-known/atproto-client-metadata.json` — client metadata (PDS fetches this) ## Type of change - [ ] Bug fix - [x] Feature (requires [approved Discussion](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/discussions/categories/ideas)) - [ ] Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] Documentation - [ ] Performance improvement - [ ] Tests - [ ] Chore (dependencies, CI, tooling) ## Checklist - [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] `pnpm typecheck` passes - [x] `pnpm --silent lint:json | jq '.diagnostics | length'` returns 0 - [x] `pnpm test` passes (or targeted tests for my change) - [x] `pnpm format` has been run - [x] I have added/updated tests for my changes (if applicable) - [x] I have added a [changeset](https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#changesets) (if this PR changes a published package) - [x] New features link to an approved Discussion: https://github.com/emdash-cms/emdash/discussions/320 ## AI-generated code disclosure - [x] This PR includes AI-generated code ## Screenshots / test output ### Test results (2026-04-08) **emdash (core):** 2096 tests, 113 files — all passing ``` Test Files 113 passed (113) Tests 2096 passed (2096) ``` **@emdash-cms/plugin-atproto:** 76 tests, 7 files — all passing ``` ✓ tests/plugin.test.ts (5 tests) 3ms ✓ tests/atproto.test.ts (3 tests) 4ms ✓ tests/auth.test.ts (15 tests) 9ms ✓ tests/standard-site.test.ts (21 tests) 5ms ✓ tests/bluesky.test.ts (18 tests) 15ms ✓ tests/resolve-handle.test.ts (3 tests) 15ms ✓ tests/oauth-client.test.ts (11 tests) 123ms Test Files 7 passed (7) Tests 76 passed (76) ``` **@emdash-cms/auth:** 41 tests, 2 files — all passing ``` Test Files 2 passed (2) Tests 41 passed (41) ``` **@emdash-cms/admin:** ⚠️ Browser tests failing due to Playwright infrastructure issue (pre-existing `@vitest/browser-playwright` setup error, not a regression from this PR).

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> I want to convert Fortran codebases to Rust using an automated conversion pipeline that leverages LLM. The pipeline has to ensure numerical accuracy between the Fortran and Rust code and achieve comparable or better performance. The first codebase is BLAS, where the first milestone is full or near-full automation of the dgemm function. The second is to go to 10 functions, and the last one is the full library.
> 
> This repository should allow someone to clone it, run a Rust conversion of the specified Fortran database code, and, optionally, for the specified subset only, receive a post-conversion report on accuracy and performance, along with the converted code.
> 
> I want to explore 3 ideas.
> 1. An LLM-first, rule-fallback.
> The core idea is to let an LLM do the heavy lifting; invoke a rule‑based transpiler only when the LLM fails to compile.
> The steps are:
>   a. Pre‑process – split Fortran into ≤ 200‑line functions, strip comments, build a call‑graph.
>   b. LLM translate – feed each function to LLM or another with a prompt that supplies external vars & intrinsics.
>   c. Compile & repair – run rustc; feed errors back to the LLM for up to 2 repair rounds.
>   d. Unit‑test round‑trip – auto‑generate Fortran‑style unit tests, run both versions, compare outputs.
>   e. Package – glue functions into a Cargo crate, run cargo test.
> Tools/Prompts:
>   - Tree‑sitter‑fortran or fparser for parsing
>   - LLM API (Start open‑source, but allow paid, like my GitHub Copilot)
>   - rustc/cargo
>   - Simple Python harness for test generation
> 
> 2. An Agentic multi‑turn dialogue.
> The core idea is to use a Questioner‑Solver agent pair (as in LLMigrate & Fortran2CPP) to catch semantic mistakes that pure one‑shot LLMs miss.
> The steps are:
>   a. Chunk & embed – same preprocessing as idea 1.
>   b. Solver – LLM proposes Rust translation.
>   c. Questioner – second LLM (or same model with a different prompt) asks clarifying questions about Fortran intrinsics, implicit typing, and module interfaces; the Solver revises.
>   d. Compile‑test loop – as in idea 1.
>   e. Idiomization pass – run a Rust‑clippy‑like script to replace unsafe blocks with safe idioms where possible.
>   f. Final audit – spot‑check < 15 % of lines.
> Tools/prompts:
>   - Two‑prompt LLM pipeline (can be done with a single model via role‑play)
>   - Same parsing & build tools as Plan 1
>   - Clippy / miri for safety checks
> 
> 3. Hybrid rule‑based + LLM polishing
> The core idea is to start with a deterministic Fortran‑to‑Rust transpiler (e.g., f2c‑style or a custom regex‑based tool) to get a compilable skeleton, then let an LLM refine idioms and ownership.
> The steps are:
>   a. Rule‑based skeleton – run a quick Fortran‑to‑C transpiler (e.g., f2c) followed by a C‑to‑Rust tool (c2rust) to produce unsafe Rust.
>   b. LLM polish – feed each unsafe function to an LLM with a prompt to replace raw pointers with Rust references, lifetimes, and proper error handling.
>   c. Compile & test – same as idea 1.
>   d. Benchmark sanity‑check – run a lightweight performance kernel (e.g., matrix‑multiply) to ensure no major regression.
>   e. Document – generate Rustdoc comments from original Fortran comments.
> Tools/prompts:
>   - f2c (or f2c‑like)
>   - c2rust (or a simple C→Rust regex mapper)
>   - LLM for polishing
>   - cargo bench/criterion for quick perf check
> 
> Since this is a demo, add a script or an executable that launches the entire process, including fetching the BLAS library and prompting the user to choose what to convert: a single function, a sample of functions, or the entire library, and which idea to use for the conversion. During the conversion, there should be processing feedback, and, depending on the idea used, questions, similar to how GitHub Copilot CLI tool works. 


</details>

head: e0a9ce03c8c1cc839eaf409e2677b9abf2017b1f
title: Implement Global Date Notes
body:
This PR implements the global date note feature, allowing users to attach descriptive notes to specific dates in their travel itinerary. These notes are displayed in the Planner view alongside scheduled locations.

closes #151 

---

## Description

This PR fully develops the `note` command and integrates it with the UI and storage layers. Unlike locations, notes are global to the date and provide a general description or reminder for that day's plan.

**Key Changes:**
- **Global Storage:** Notes are now stored in a centralized `Map<VisitDate, NoteContent>` within the `AddressBook`, making them independent of individual location records.
- **Reactive UI:** The `PlannerListPanel` now dynamically observes a `plannerNote` property in the `Model`. When a user runs the `plan` command, the UI automatically updates to show the relevant note.
- **Smart Note Merging:** If multiple notes apply to the same date (e.g., a specific date note and a recurring "Every Friday" note), they are intelligently merged and displayed together.
- **Persistence:** Global notes are serialized into `addressbook.json` and persist across application restarts.
- **Undo/Redo Support:** The `note` command is now fully undoable, integrated into the application's state-snapshot mechanism.

---

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [x] Backend implementation (fulfilling deferred functionality)
- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Documentation update (Implementation details in Developer Guide)

---

## Test Coverage
- ✅ **Unit Tests:** Updated `NoteCommandTest` to verify backend execution and `AddressBookTest` for map serialization.
- ✅ **Mocking:** Updated `ModelStub` in `AddCommandTest` to support new interface methods.
- ✅ **Integration Tests:** Verified that `NoteCommand` correctly modifies the model and triggers UI-bound properties.

### Manual Testing Verification
- `note n/buy souvenir d/2026-03-24` → Success message shown.
- `plan 2026-03-24` → Planner sidebar displays "buy souvenir".
- `undo` → Note disappears from the active planner view.
- Restart App → `plan 2026-03-24` still shows the saved note.
- `note n/Weekly check d/every Tuesday` → Note displays every Tuesday in the planner.


---

## Checklist for Reviewers

- [x] Code follows the project's coding style (Checkstyle passed)
- [x] Comments and documentation are clear and accurate
- [x] All tests pass locally
- [x] New feature is fully integrated with Undo/Redo
- [x] Storage uses `toDataString()` to ensure robust cross-session loading
- [x] UI placeholder "TEST" removed and replaced with live data bindings
- [x] Multiple notes for the same `LocalDate` handle string joining correctly

---

## Future Enhancements

Possible improvements for future iterations:
- Implementation of `DeleteNoteCommand` (currently deferred)
- Support for rich text or bullet points in notes
- Adding an "Edit Note" button directly in the Planner UI
- Visual indicators/icons in the list view for dates that have notes attached

title: Persistent named palettes with tabbed drawer, export, and UX polish
body:
Replaces the flat auto-history drawer with a tabbed palette system: a persistent auto-history palette at index 0, plus user-created named palettes. Several behavioral bugs were caught and fixed across iterative review.

## Data layer
- New `Palette` model (`id`, `name?`, `pairs`, `createdAt`); auto-history is `palettes[0]` where `name == nil`
- `migrateHistoryToPalettes()` merges legacy `colorHistory` into `palettes[0].pairs` rather than overwriting
- `Defaults[.activePaletteIndex]` tracks the active tab; clamped to 0 on out-of-range

## Palette management (`Eyedroppers`)
- `savePalette`, `renamePalette`, `deletePalette`, `addCurrentToPalette`, `deleteChipFromPalette`
- `swap()` only calls `pushUndo()` when on auto-history (index 0) — named-palette swaps no longer corrupt the undo stack
- `savePalette` sets `activeHistoryID = current.id` so the new chip is selected immediately
- `deleteChipFromPalette` nils `activeHistoryID` when the removed pair was active
- `deletePalette` calls `restoreAutoHistorySelection()` after clamping to index 0, and decrements `activePaletteIndex` when deleting a palette before the active one

## Drawer UI
- `PaletteTabBar` with inline create/rename via `PaletteNameField`; auto-history tab shows a clock icon
- Tab switch uses directional vertical slide — `slideDirection` is set via `@Binding` in the button action *before* `activePaletteIndex` changes, avoiding the one-frame-behind issue that `onChange` caused
- `isAutoHistory` derived from `activePalette?.isAutoHistory ?? false`; `activePaletteIndex` is clamped back to 0 async when out of range
- Context-menu remove label switches between `textHistoryRemove` and `textPaletteRemoveChip` based on `isAutoHistory`

## Export
- `Exporter.paletteToJSON` serialises pairs; auto-history entries include an ISO 8601 `date` field
- `ISO8601DateFormatter` hoisted out of the `pairs.map` closure (one allocation per export, not per pair)
- Filename strips `/`, `:`, `\` before `NSSavePanel`; write errors surface via `NSAlert`

## UI polish
- Toolbar tooltips include keyboard shortcuts: preview (P), compliance (C), history (H)
- Compliance button: `checkmark.shield.fill` when active vs `checkmark.shield` when inactive

head: b462b109b630dd1e1a9a78088b18429d2baaae9b
title: Fix two reviewer-flagged issues: invalid parquet arg & checkpoint opt-in
body:
Two issues identified in code review:

- **Invalid `pd.read_parquet` argument** — `index=False` is not a valid parameter and raises at runtime when reading Parquet inputs.
- **Checkpoint written by default** — `checkpoint_path` was uncommented in `config.yaml`, silently enabling checkpointing for all users and potentially writing files outside `out_dir`.

## Changes

- **`protein_intensities.py`**: Remove `index=False` from `pd.read_parquet`; index is already set via `.set_index(index_col)`.
  ```python
  # Before
  data = pd.read_parquet(input_intensities, index=False, engine='fastparquet').set_index(index_col)
  # After
  data = pd.read_parquet(input_intensities, engine='fastparquet').set_index(index_col)
  ```
- **`config.yaml`**: Comment out `checkpoint_path` so checkpointing is opt-in.
  ```yaml
  # checkpoint_path: 'checkpoint.pt'
  ```

head: e1477f8b3f18c1de6ff87dbca9465a7b106dc193
title: Fix staleness filter for NO variance strategy
body:
## Summary

The staleness filter was removing 77 of 83 eligible markets because their prices hadn't changed in 5 cycles. For a BUY NO variance strategy, stable prices with active volume represent persistent mispricings — the ideal opportunity, not staleness.

Changed the staleness signal from "price unchanged" to "no trading activity": a market is stale only when price is unchanged AND volume is below a floor (default 10) AND open interest hasn't changed. Markets with stable prices but active trading now pass through correctly.

- Replaced `volume_spike_ratio` parameter with `volume_floor` (minimum volume to consider active)
- Added `open_interest` tracking to StalenessEntry for OI-change detection
- Backward compatible with existing `scan_staleness.json` files (old entries missing `open_interest` default to 0)

Closes #467

title: Add ping utilities
body:
This pull request enhances the `DeviceMonitoringService` by improving support for ICMP ping functionality, especially in containerized environments. The main changes ensure that the necessary system package is installed in the Docker image and that the service gracefully handles unsupported platform scenarios.

Dependency updates for ping support:

* Updated the Dockerfile (`src/API/Dockerfile`) to install `iputils-ping`, ensuring ICMP ping commands work inside the container.

Error handling improvements:

* Added a catch for `PlatformNotSupportedException` in `PingDeviceAsync` that logs a warning (at most once per service lifetime) when ping is not supported on the current platform. A thread-safe guard flag using `Interlocked.CompareExchange` prevents log spam when devices are checked in parallel.
* The `iputils-ping` / `CAP_NET_RAW` guidance is placed in the `PingException` catch path, where it is most relevant.

Code cleanup:

head: 8fc7cd32904240c2c841e70aef2ba5c3bb659ffd
title: Add resolution support for image formats (JPEG, TIFF, PNG, BMP) along with unit parsing
body:
Solution for https://github.com/sdsykes/fastimage/issues/164

### Summary

- Adds `FastImage.resolution(uri)` class method returning `[[x, y], :units]` or `nil`
- Adds `#resolution` and `#resolution_units` instance methods returning the components separately
- Supports JPEG (JFIF APP0), PNG (pHYs chunk), BMP (DIB header), and TIFF (EXIF IFD rational tags)
- Extends `GoodFixtures` with a resolution column and adds a `test_should_report_resolution_correctly` sweep test covering all fixture files

### Supported formats and units

| Format | Source | Possible units |
|--------|--------|----------------|
| JPEG | JFIF APP0 segment | `:inches`, `:centimeters`, `:no_units` |
| PNG | pHYs chunk | `:meters`, `:no_units` |
| BMP | DIB header (`XPelsPerMeter`/`YPelsPerMeter`) | `:meters` |
| TIFF | EXIF `XResolution`/`YResolution` rational tags | `:inches`, `:centimeters`, `:no_units` |

Formats without resolution metadata (GIF, WebP, SVG, HEIC, AVIF, JXL, PSD, ICO) return `nil` for both methods.

### API

```ruby
# Class method — returns [[x, y], :units] or nil
FastImage.resolution("image.jpg")  # => [[72, 72], :inches]
FastImage.resolution("image.png")  # => nil

# Instance methods
fi = FastImage.new("image.tiff")
fi.resolution        # => [72.0, 72.0]
fi.resolution_units  # => :inches
```

### Notes

- TIFF resolution values are `Float` (stored as RATIONAL numerator/denominator in EXIF); other formats return `Integer`
- BMP returns `nil` when both PPM values are zero (unspecified) or when the file uses the older `BITMAPCOREHEADER` which has no resolution fields
- The EXIF parser was extended with named tag/data-type constants and a two-pass approach to read RATIONAL offsets after the IFD scan
